stocks.note: Numbers as of market close May 1st.
stocks.news:
GameStop (GME +6.33%) is reportedly weighing a bid for eBay (EBAY +0.57%). GME has roughly $9B in cash against a ~$12B market cap, while eBay sits near $46B. CEO Ryan Cohen wants to run the same playbook he used at Chewy years back. Whether shareholders buy the comparison is the open question.

FedEx (FDX -2.39%) and UPS (UPS -1.13%) said they will pass tariff refunds back to customers. Roughly $166B is now refundable after February's Supreme Court ruling unwound the Trump tariff program, and the cash is already showing up in earnings at importers like GM (GM -1.46%). Money flowing back to the people who actually paid it usually finds its way into hiring or spending.

economy.note: US 10-Year and Gold as of 4:00 PM ET May 3rd; WTI Crude reflects today's intraday move via investing.com.
economy.commentary:
🏛️ U.S. debt held by the public just outpaced GDP for the first time since 1946. GDP printed at $31.22 trillion in March. Public debt came in at $31.27 trillion. The CBO's baseline expects the line to keep climbing past 106% by 2030.
Recreated by REALTY EXPERTS® · Source: CBO Long-Term Budget Outlook · Treasury Historical Tables
This is the kind of macro number that sets the floor under mortgage rates for the rest of the decade. More government borrowing means more competition for the same dollar pool that funds mortgages. That pressure does not ease quickly. Rates can drift, but the structural gravity here pulls upward. The UAW is holding a strike vote at Stellantis's (STLA -2.06%) Ram 1500 plant in Michigan this week, ~6,000 workers. The union's beef: contract work moved off union rosters. About 300,000 U.S. workers struck in 2025, up 13% year over year, so this is part of a bigger pattern. Crude pushed up sharply today: WTI sits around $105.48, +3.47% on the day. The European luxury picture in Market Briefs ties straight to this, since Group III base oil prices in northern Europe have nearly doubled since the Iran conflict began. Gold ticked down 0.61% to $4,616 as some safe-haven money rotated.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET on May 3rd.
crypto.commentary:
Crypto opened the week green across all three majors. The bigger story is policy: the CLARITY Act, the major U.S. crypto bill that's been stuck for months, just cleared its biggest holdup according to Coinbase (COIN +1.85%). Lawmakers compromised on stablecoin yield rules, the piece that had been blocking everything else. Now the bill heads to a Senate vote.

Meanwhile Tether is now the largest known gold holder outside of central banks and nation states. They added 6+ tons in Q1 to push reserves to roughly 132 tons, about $19.8B. Per JPMorgan (JPM -0.24%), that's more gold than any central bank except Poland through 2025. A stablecoin issuer is now effectively running its own central-bank reserve strategy.

real_estate.homebuilder: Cycles End, Cycles Begin: Where The Spring Buyers Actually Showed Up
real_estate.commentary:
Spirit Airlines flew off into the sunset this weekend after a $5.5B peak in 2014 ended in shutdown. Cycles end. Cycles begin. Locally the spring rebound is real but uneven, the same story Market Briefs is tracking nationally: home prices fell in 39 of America's 129 biggest metros early this year, mostly Florida and the Sun Belt, while Detroit jumped 17% as Rust Belt cities pull demand back.

Lower prices plus rates that have come down from last year's highs could mean a stronger spring, but only in the markets where buyers actually show up. The 30-year sits at 6.44%, the 15-year at 6.01%. Buyers who are at the door right now have already accepted the rate environment. They're qualified and committed.

For listing agents: the qualified buyer pool is the smallest it's been in two years, but it's also the most committed. They've accepted the rate. Price for that buyer, not for the rate-cut buyer who isn't coming.
